query: What problem does PagedAttention solve in LLM serving?
answer:
**PagedAttention addresses the memory‑bound bottleneck that limits large‑language‑model (LLM) serving.**  
When an LLM processes long contexts, the traditional attention mechanism must hold the entire key/value tensors in contiguous GPU memory. This quickly exhausts GPU RAM, forcing model truncation or slower, multi‑step swapping. PagedAttention reorganizes these tensors into a set of smaller, page‑aligned blocks that can be fetched on demand. The result is a dramatic reduction in peak memory usage while preserving, or even improving, throughput. In practice, the technique enables a 3.58× higher throughput compared to Orca on the same hardware, as shown in recent benchmarks [[1]](https://aeronation-rag-test-log-and-chat-history.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/pdfs/2309.06180v1.pdf).
